note: All tracks are field recordings of rara bands on the road or at their temples (Croix-des-Bouquets, Bizoton, Carrefour du Fort, Cité Soleil, Artibonite, 1930s–1990s) and of Haitian gagá bands in Dominican cane towns; years are release years, the recordings are older (Lomax 1936–37, Gillis 1976–78, McAlister 1993). Rasin bands that borrow rara horns are left to Mizik rasin.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Published rara is almost all field recording: Folkways FE 4531 (1978, four LP sides), its CD Caribbean Revels (1991, 14 tracks), one volume of the Lomax Haiti box (2009, about 30 short items from 1936–37), two tracks on Rhythms of Rapture (1995), two Stearns tracks on Songs and Dances of Haiti (1952) and Soul Jazz's Rara in Haiti (2010, 12 songs in three medleys). Behind that sit hundreds of bands (Haitian Creole Wikipedia: over 30 in Léogâne alone) whose new songs each season circulate on local cassettes, radio and video, mostly uncatalogued, plus diaspora rara in New York. An insider's essential list is about 25 recordings.
